production.title: Claude Artifacts Just Got a Huge Upgrade

narration:
Claude just dropped a feature that allows you to install an artifact
as a real app right on your Mac or Windows computer.
So that little tracker or dashboard that you or your team use,
Claude can now build that right on your desktop.
So in this video, I’m going to show you how these new apps work,
the other big upgrades that make artifacts one of the most
important Claude features to be getting good at right now,
and the real risk of getting locked into Claude’s ecosystem.
So let’s get right into it.
An installed artifact gets its own desktop icon
and window instead of opening inside Claude.
The way this works is you actually build an artifact just like normal.
And then when you open it up inside of the Claude desktop app,
you just go to share or you click on the name of the artifact,
and then you can hit install as app,
and then it gets its own icon and it opens up in its
own window like any other app on your actual laptop or desktop.
This app can still use Claude and all of your connectors.
It can send you notifications or sit in
your menu bar or your system tray,
and it updates itself whenever you actually update the artifact.
There’s no API key or anything else to set up.
Now, right now it is in beta, and it literally just dropped.
And anything made from a template like your docs, slides,
or sheets can’t be installed.
And if an app asks you for access to your computer,
like running programs or changing local files,
only allow it for apps you built or
really trust because Anthropic doesn’t automatically review these.
But anyways, apps are just the newest upgrade to artifacts.
Over the last few months,
Anthropic has turned artifacts into something that your
whole team can really work out of.
And people have made more than 45 million
docs or decks and designs with artifacts.
Anthropic defines an artifact as anything that Claude makes
for you that you’d put in front of someone, like a design, a deck,
a doc, a dashboard, or maybe a small interactive tool.
Basically, it’s a page that Claude builds that lives at a live public link.
And right now, there are 7 templates.
We’ve got docs, slides, design, data, sheets, whiteboards, and motion for short animated explainers.
And then every update that you make is
just a new version of that same link.
The hard part here was never getting Claude to be able to make something.
But now with Artifacts, you can just have Claude build it,
and then you can hit share,
and then your team just opens up a link, and it’s super simple.
I don’t think that artifacts will replace Excel or your CRM,
at least not yet.
Anthropic even says Sheets only has simple spreadsheet functionality for now.
And if you need a real app with real
login and real backend and real role-based access control,
then you’ll probably want to go with something that you actually
deploy yourself or some other solution that’s built for that.
What I think Artifacts replaces is like the small software, right?
Like every team has little things they either
pay a subscription for or never build,
like a hiring tracker or an onboarding checklist or
a training quiz or a weekly KPI page,
or I think you guys get the picture, right?
And now each one is basically just a prompt and a link.
And then just tell Claude,
“Turn this into a shared artifact that my team can open from a link.
Make it easy to update every week and show where every number came from.”
And now the last thing I wanted to address,
because some of you might be thinking,
if everything about your business lives inside of Claude, like as an artifact,
aren’t you just locking yourself into Claude Code or into Anthropic?
And it’s a very fair concern.
Artifact content, yes, it is stored on Anthropic’s infrastructure.
People in your organization have to sign into Claude to see it.
Every big AI company is kind of doing some version
of this because they’re realizing the model alone might not
be the moat heading into the next couple of years.
So they’re all building the place where your work actually lives.
But of course,
all of these artifacts have their own sort of like exit door.
You can export them to Word or PDF or Google Docs or PowerPoint slides,
Sheets, CSV, HTML, whatever you want.
The rule for these artifacts is pretty simple,
which is basically just keep the source of truth in places
you own and then just use artifacts as the window.
It’s less about Claude-specific artifacts.
It’s really more about knowing how to brief
AI to build what your team needs, how to check it,
how to share it,
how to get people working from a link instead of a file.
And I think that all of these skills will
carry over to whatever tool ends up winning.
Bet on the habit and the skill of
working that way rather than one specific tool.
Follow us for more.

research.summary: Anthropic released “Install as app” for Claude Artifacts on November 24, 2026. The beta lets users turn eligible artifacts into Mac or Windows desktop apps with their own icons and windows. Installed apps can use Claude and connected apps, update when the underlying artifact changes, send notifications, add menu-bar or system-tray items, and—when explicitly permitted—access local files or run programs. The core feature is real, but the video’s broader plan details need correction: template availability differs by plan, installed apps require Claude Desktop version 6.28899.0 or later, and Docs, Slides, Sheets, legacy artifacts, and Claude Cowork live artifacts cannot be installed as apps.

claims.claim: Claude released “Install as app” for Artifacts on November 24, 2026, in beta for Mac and Windows.
claims.source_title: Turn artifacts into Mac and Windows apps

claims.claim: An installed artifact gets its own desktop icon and window instead of opening inside Claude, and the installation flow is available from the artifact’s title menu, right-click menu, or Share menu.
claims.source_title: Install an artifact as an app

claims.claim: Installing artifacts as apps is rolling out in beta on Free, Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, and Enterprise plans, but users need Claude for Mac or Claude for Windows version 6.28899.0 or later.
claims.source_title: Install an artifact as an app

claims.claim: Installed apps can use Claude and a user’s connected apps, and they can update automatically when the underlying artifact is edited.
claims.source_title: Turn artifacts into Mac and Windows apps

claims.claim: With permission, an installed artifact can send notifications, add a macOS menu-bar item or Windows system-tray item, run programs, and read, change, or delete local files.
claims.source_title: Install an artifact as an app

claims.claim: Anthropic warns that it does not review apps before installation; full computer access should therefore be granted only to apps whose creators the user trusts.
claims.source_title: Turn artifacts into Mac and Windows apps

claims.claim: Installed apps do not require packaging, code signing, an API key, or a separate login, but they do require the user to be online and signed in to Claude Desktop to open them.
claims.source_title: Install an artifact as an app

claims.claim: Docs, Slides, Sheets, legacy artifacts, and live artifacts from Claude Cowork cannot be installed as desktop apps at launch; apps are also unavailable on Linux, the web, and mobile.
claims.source_title: Install an artifact as an app

claims.claim: Claude defines an artifact as something it creates that a user would put in front of someone else, including a design, deck, document, dashboard, or small interactive tool.
claims.source_title: What are artifacts and how do I use them?

claims.claim: Artifacts can call Claude without users supplying API keys; usage is charged against each user’s own plan limits rather than the artifact creator’s limits.
claims.source_title: What are artifacts and how do I use them?

claims.claim: Artifacts can connect to services such as Asana, Google Calendar, and Slack, subject to the user’s approval and plan availability.
claims.source_title: What are artifacts and how do I use them?

claims.claim: Artifacts can store persistent personal or shared data, enabling use cases such as journals, trackers, collaborative tools, and leaderboards; the default storage limit is 100 MB or 25,000 saved records, whichever is reached first.
claims.source_title: What are artifacts and how do I use them?

claims.claim: Anthropic says users have created more than 45 million documents, decks, and designs in Claude, and that teams can edit the same document, deck, design, or dashboard together.
claims.source_title: Build live dashboards and animate explainers with Claude

claims.claim: The current artifact templates listed by Anthropic are Docs, Slides, Design, Data, Sheets, Whiteboards, and Motion; availability varies by plan, with Docs, Slides, and Design available on all plans, Data on paid plans, Sheets and Whiteboards in beta on paid plans, and Motion in beta on Team and Enterprise.
claims.source_title: What are artifacts and how do I use them?

claims.claim: The video’s lock-in concern has a factual basis: artifact apps run through Anthropic’s infrastructure, and installed apps require an active Claude Desktop session and Claude account access rather than functioning as fully independent offline applications.
claims.source_title: What are artifacts and how do I use them?

core_fact.fact: On November 24, 2026, Claude introduced a beta feature that lets users install eligible Artifacts as Mac or Windows desktop apps with their own icons and windows. The apps can use Claude and connected tools, update when the artifact changes, and request permission for operating-system access.

metadata.title: Claude Artifacts Just Became Real Desktop Apps
metadata.description:
Claude Artifacts can now become real desktop apps on Mac and Windows, and this video shows how Claude apps work, what they can replace, and the risks to know first.

Free guide to this video (steps and every source): https://studio.golidee.com/guides/golide-long-2026-11-26.pdf

You’ll see how to install an Artifact as an app with its own icon and window, use Claude connectors and notifications, and build simple tools for your team without setting up an API key. The feature is still in beta, so there are important limits and security concerns to understand.

We also look at whether Claude Artifacts can replace spreadsheets, CRMs, hiring trackers, dashboards, checklists, and other small business tools—and how to avoid getting locked into Claude by keeping your source of truth somewhere you control.

Chapters
0:00 Intro
0:32 Installed Apps
1:29 Artifact Basics
2:21 Small Team Tools
3:14 Lock-In Risk

#Claude #ClaudeAI #ClaudeArtifacts #AIApps #Anthropic #AIAutomation #Productivity

Music: Crock Pot by Diamond Ortiz
